bug_semantics: A RECORD user who can SELECT a table with an array-element SELECT permission (DEFINE FIELD items[*] / field.* PERMISSIONS FOR select) still sees a subset of denied elements. The three filter sites (reduce_document / filter_computed_field_permissions in doc/reduce.rs, the post-projection pass in doc/output.rs, and filter_fields_by_permission in exec/operators/scan/pipeline.rs) expand the field idiom with Value::each, which yields ascending array-index paths, then Value::cut (historically Value::del) does Vec::remove at each index. Removing while walking forwards shifts every later index down, so a deny-all leaks the odd-indexed elements and a per-element WHERE keeps/drops the wrong identities. Non-wildcard field-level SELECT permissions are enforced correctly; root and record-owner sessions skip this filter.

reasoning: GHSA-8rw6-p7m8-63jp is a live reviewed advisory (withdrawn_at null; GitHub/OSV aliases empty and nvd_published_at null, so no CVE.org record to contradict the vendor GHSA). The sink is real: RECORD-user SELECT of an array whose element field has PERMISSIONS FOR select walks each()-expanded indices and Vec::remove()s denied slots forwards, leaking odd-indexed or mis-predicated elements. The smallest public first-write of that loop is c4386f1549baed416e8add1dc7498532d3777b19 in pluck.rs; the parent tree lacks the loop; DEFINE FIELD already allowed .* / [*] and each()/del() already implemented ascending expand + index remove. Subsequent file splits, del-to-cut, and the 2026 pipeline wildcard copy are refactors/carriers (a squash/move is not a BIC). The BIC commit object is human-only (Tobie Morgan Hitchcock, no AI trailer/bot). A later Claude co-author on 15579bd2c is ignored for attribution. The advisory fix SHA 8f89b260b is the mainline reverse-iteration patch; 6881b18 is the same patch on 3.1.4. Verdict NOT_AI.
